The gun you choose should be dependable and safe. The fewer levers and buttons on it the better.

Consider a shotgun. They're the most versatile. Best type for shooting sports, can hunt anything in North America with one, and arguably the best option for home defense. There are dozens of popular chamberings for rifles and handguns, and one rifle or handgun will usually only set you up to use one of them. Most shotguns use the same gauge and accept the same shells (12 gauge), and most of the rest use one of the others (20 gauge). They also run about half the cost of handguns and rifles of comparable quality, and while there are plenty of duds in the handgun and rifle market, you can't really go wrong with many of the shotgun options out there.

Try to find a range that allows you to rent a gun and shoot it before you buy. Another good thing is to put lots of guns in your hands and see what feels right and what doesn't. Gun manufacturing has come a long way and generally customer service is great.

If you're new to guns, you'll really want to take a class. This is great, because any well-run class will have guns there for you to use, and you can try different kinds and see what you like best.
